paper.title: DCM Bandits: Learning to Rank with Multiple Clicks

unmapped: Actions are ordered lists of m (paper's K) items out of K (paper's L) items; dependent click model with item attraction probabilities and position termination probabilities
Reward (user satisfaction) is unobserved; learner observes click vector only (cascade-like feedback)
Learner knows the order of the termination probabilities
Optimal solution as a set assumed unique
settings.definition_quote: We refer to our learning problem as a \emph{DCM bandit}. Formally, we define it as a tuple $B = (E, P_\textsc{w}, P_\textsc{v}, K)$, where $E = [L]$ is a \emph{ground set} of $L$ items; $P_\textsc{w}$ and $P_\textsc{v}$ are probability distributions over $\set{0, 1}^E$ and $\set{0, 1}^K$, respectively; and $K \leq L$ is the number of recommended items.

unmapped: Actions are ordered lists of m (paper's K) items out of K (paper's L) items; dependent click model
Hard instances B_LB with identical termination probabilities gamma
settings.definition_quote: Our lower bound is derived on the following class of problems. The ground set are $L$ items $E = [L]$ and $K$ of these items are optimal ... The number of positions is $K$ and their termination probabilities are identical, $\bar{v}(k) = \gamma$ for all positions $k \in [K]$.

bound.expression_latex: R_i(n) \leq \sum_{e = i + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, i} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, i}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(i)}} (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + i L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 i \log \log n

symbols.G_i: sum_{e=i+1}^{L} Delta_{e,i}(1+log(1/Delta_{e,i})) / kl(w(e), w(i)), with Delta_{e,i} = w(i) - w(e) attraction-probability gap

tuning: UCB threshold log t + 3 log log t

source.label: thm:cascade regret
source.quote: For any $i \in [K]$ and $\eps > 0$, the expected $n$-step cascade regret of $\dcmklucb$ is bounded as R_i(n) \leq \sum_{e = i + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, i} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, i}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(i)}} \times (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C, where $C = i L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 i \log \log n$

results.notes: Bound on the auxiliary 'cascade regret' R_i(n), not the DCM regret; quantity set to other. Paper's L is canonical K (number of items), paper's K is m.

bound.expression_latex: R(n) \leq \frac{\gamma}{\alpha} \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, K} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, K}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(K)}} (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + \frac{\gamma}{\alpha} \left(K L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 K \log \log n\right)

conditions: all termination probabilities equal: v(k) = gamma for all k

source.label: thm:simple upper bound
source.quote: Let $\bar{v}(k) = \gamma$ for all $k \in [K]$ and $\eps > 0$. Then the expected $n$-step regret of $\dcmklucb$ is bounded as R(n) \leq \frac{\gamma}{\alpha} \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, K} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, K}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(K)}} \times (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C, where $C = \frac{\gamma}{\alpha} \left(K L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 K \log \log n\right)$

results.notes: Regret defined as E[sum f(A*,w_t,v_t) - f(A_t,w_t,v_t)], which equals expected difference of means (could be classified pseudo_regret). Paper's L = canonical K, paper's K = m.

bound.expression_latex: R(n) \leq (1 + \eps) \sum_{i = 1}^K \frac{\bar{v}(i) - \bar{v}(i + 1)}{\alpha} \sum_{e = i + 1}^L \frac{\Delta_{e, i} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, i}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(i)}} (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C

symbols.H_v: sum_{i=1}^{m} (v(i) - v(i+1))/alpha_dcm * sum_{e=i+1}^{L} Delta_{e,i}(1+log(1/Delta_{e,i}))/kl(w(e), w(i)), with v(m+1)=0

conditions: termination probabilities ordered v(1) >= ... >= v(m), order known to learner

source.label: thm:upper bound
source.quote: Let $\bar{v}(1) \geq \ldots \geq \bar{v}(K)$ and $\eps > 0$. Then the expected $n$-step regret of $\dcmklucb$ is bounded as R(n) \leq (1 + \eps) \sum_{i = 1}^K \frac{\bar{v}(i) - \bar{v}(i + 1)}{\alpha} \times \sum_{e = i + 1}^L \frac{\Delta_{e, i} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, i}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(i)}} (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C, where $\bar{v}(K + 1) = 0$ ...

results.notes: Reduces to Theorem 1 when all v(k)=gamma.

conditions: instance class B_LB: m optimal items with attraction p, others p - Delta, all termination probabilities equal gamma

source.label: thm:lower bound
source.quote: For any DCM bandit $B_\mathrm{LB}$, the regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded from below as \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{R(n)}{\log n} \geq \gamma \alpha \frac{(L - K) \Delta}{\kl{p - \Delta}{p}}.

results.notes: Consistency defined via E[T_n(e)] = o(n^a) for suboptimal items. Paper's L = canonical K, paper's K = m. Paper notes upper bound of Thm 1 matches up to log(1/Delta) when p = 1/m.
